title: The twisting sheaf O(1) on P^n_Z on the standard charts
statement: Let $n\ge0$, $S=\mathbf Z[T_0,\dots,T_n]$ graded by total degree, $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj] with standard opens $D_+(T_j)$ and $\Gamma(D_+(f),\mathcal O)=S_{(f)}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and $\mathcal O(1)=\widetilde{S(1)}$ the $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}$-module attached to the shifted graded module $S(1)$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (so $\mathcal O(1)(D_+(f))=S(1)_{(f)}=(S_f)_1$ for homogeneous $f$ of positive degree), with the global sections $T_0,\dots,T_n\in\Gamma(\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z},\mathcal O(1))$ given by $T_l\mapsto T_l/1\in(S_f)_1$ on every $D_+(f)$. Then: (i) $\mathcal O(1)$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]; more precisely, for every $j$ the map $\mathcal O_{D_+(T_j)}\to\mathcal O(1)|_{D_+(T_j)}$, $a\mapsto a\cdot T_j|$, is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{D_+(T_j)}$-modules, and the $D_+(T_j)$ cover $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$; (ii) for every $j$, $D_+(T_j)\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_{(T_j)}$ and $S_{(T_j)}=\mathbf Z[T_0/T_j,\dots,T_n/T_j]$ is the polynomial ring over $\mathbf Z$ in the $n$ elements $T_l/T_j$, $l\neq j$; (iii) $D_+(T_j)$ is the non-vanishing locus $(\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z})_{T_j}=\{x: T_{j,x}\notin\mathfrak m_x\mathcal O(1)_x\}$ of the section $T_j$ ($\mathfrak m_x$ the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z},x}$ [def-weil-residue-field]); (iv) for all $j,l$, $T_l|_{D_+(T_j)}=(T_l/T_j)\cdot T_j|_{D_+(T_j)}$ in $\mathcal O(1)(D_+(T_j))$, where $T_l/T_j\in S_{(T_j)}=\Gamma(D_+(T_j),\mathcal O)$; (v) $\mathcal O(1)$ is canonically the glued module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] for $A=\mathbf Z$, $d=1$: if $\mathcal L$ is that module, with bases $e_j$ of $\mathcal L|_{D_+(T_j)}$ and $e_i=(T_i/T_j)e_j$ on $D_+(T_i)\cap D_+(T_j)$, there is a unique isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}$-modules $\Phi:\mathcal L\to\mathcal O(1)$ with $\Phi(e_j)=T_j|_{D_+(T_j)}$ for all $j$, and $\Phi$ carries the global section $x_l$ of $\mathcal L$ given by $(T_l/T_j)e_j$ on each $D_+(T_j)$ to $T_l$.

proof.text: Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top' applied to the degree-one variables and MvPolynomial.adjoin_range_X_eq_top gives the standard-open cover. Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec gives each affine chart. The inverse of homogeneousLocalizationAwayXEquiv and homogeneousLocalizationAwayXEquiv_symm_X give the polynomial coordinate ring and its required values.

Use Proj.isInvertible_twist_homogeneousSubmodule and the existing isomorphism instance for the restriction of Proj.unitToTwist to D_+(T_j). These are the source library's proved degree-one twisting-sheaf trivializations; no new graded-module sheaf is constructed.

The private nonvanishingLocus_app_one identifies a module morphism from the unit with homOfGlobalSection of its value at 1, using unitHomEquiv and naturality. Apply nonvanishingLocus_eq_compl_support_zeroLocus and Proj.compl_support_zeroLocus_unitToTwist, with the homogeneous degree-one cover, to obtain nonvanishing = D_+(T_j).
Proj.map_unitToTwist_eq_smul computes T_l = (T_l/T_j) T_j on D_+(T_j); awayXRatio is the named homogeneous fraction and one_smul supplies the degree-one condition, including l=j.

Specialize the existing, proved Proj.existsUnique_polynomial_twist_glued_identification to the finite nonempty index type Fin(n+1). Its conclusion is precisely the required unique comparison with both chart and global coordinate compatibility. X_mem_homogeneousSubmodule_one and isHomogeneous_X express the same degree-one membership. No new comparison or open obligation is introduced.
